conventions.convention: There are m ≥ 1 compartments. In p_ij, j is the donor and i is the recipient; p_ij = d_ji, diagonal transfers vanish, and total mass is the unweighted coordinate sum. External sources and sinks are excluded.
Modified Patankar Euler requires an input in Ω+, h > 0, and strictly positive declared denominators. The standard accuracy choice is σ_i = y_i; zero denominators are rejected before rate evaluation.
The boundary extension assumes the additional factorization p_ij(y) = y_j a_ij(y), with C² factors on an open neighborhood and nonnegativity required only on its nonnegative states.
MPRK22(1) uses a standard Patankar Euler stage z and final off-diagonal coefficients (p_ij(y) + p_ij(z))/(2z_j). It accepts strictly positive inputs and checks z ∈ Ω+ before evaluating rates at z.

The local defect is method output minus exact next state, measured in the Euclidean norm. Accuracy and one-step stability require the stated smooth positive neighborhood; preservation alone supplies no compact positive tube.

The residual certificate concerns the exact real system represented by the stored matrix and right-hand side. Residual evaluation must satisfy the operationwise normal-intermediate hypotheses, certificate norms must be exact or upper bounds, and assembly/data errors require separate allowances.
Global convergence uses T > 0, a uniform grid h = T/N with N ≥ 1, exact initial data, and constants independent of N, conditional on the stated common compact positive tube.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite real m × m matrix with m ≥ 1, positive diagonal, nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and strict column diagonal dominance, M is invertible and M⁻¹ is entrywise nonnegative. It maps nonnegative vectors to nonnegative vectors and strictly positive vectors to strictly positive vectors.
A finite conservative PDS has F_i(y) = Σ_j(p_ij(y) − d_ij(y)), rates nonnegative on Ω+, identities p_ij = d_ji and p_ii = d_ii = 0, and total mass M(y) = Σ_i y_i.

For a finite conservative PDS, input yⁿ ∈ Ω+, h > 0, and any positive denominators, modified Patankar Euler is uniquely defined, has nonnegative output, and preserves the coordinate sum. Strictly positive input gives strictly positive output. No order claim is made for arbitrary denominators.

On the stated bounded open convex positive U with closure contained in a positive open V carrying C² rates and bounded derivatives through order two, the standard-denominator step has uniform exact-start defect at most Ch² for the stated compact-tube segments and satisfies ||Φ_h(u) − Φ_h(v)||₂ ≤ (1 + Lh)||u − v||₂ for all u,v ∈ U and 0 < h ≤ h₀.

With the stated C² source-factored representation near compact nonnegative K, every input in K and h > 0 gives a unique nonnegative, mass-conservative factorized step. Its exact-start defect is uniformly O(h²) when the exact segments remain in the stated fixed compact nonnegative subset of the factorization neighborhood; no boundary global error bound is asserted.

For strictly positive admissible input and h > 0, if the Patankar Euler stage z belongs to Ω+, the MPRK22(1) stage and output are uniquely defined, strictly positive, and preserve total mass. Otherwise the algorithm returns rate-domain-failure before its second rate evaluation.

Under the stated bounded convex positive U, positive neighborhood V, and C² bounded-rate-derivative hypotheses, sufficiently small MPRK22(1) steps have uniform exact-start defect at most Ch³ for exact segments in compact subsets of U and satisfy ||Ψ_h(u) − Ψ_h(v)||₂ ≤ (1 + Lh)||u − v||₂ for all u,v ∈ U.

Under its stored-system and successful certified-residual hypotheses, ρ bounds ||Mŷ − b||₂, mass drift is at most √m ρ, and ||ŷ − M⁻¹b||₁ ≤ √m ρ. The componentwise condition ŷ_i ≥ √m ρ certifies nonnegativity of the exact solution; a residual bound alone does not certify the candidate's nonnegativity.

seams_checked.note: The residual ledger preserves the rounded-residual supplier's stored-input, sequential-evaluation, unit-roundoff, normal-intermediate, exact-zero, and certified-norm qualifications. Assembly errors are explicitly separate.
The local lemmas use method-output-minus-exact-next-state defect, O(h²) and O(h³) for orders one and two, and the supplier's 1 + Lh input-stability convention.

Both global applications retain the fixed uniform grid, exact initial data, uniform local constants, and common compact-tube conditions. They use p = 1 or p = 2 and preserve both L > 0 and L = 0 recurrence cases.
The forward-Euler counterexample uses R(z) = 1 + z and the conditional local-order statement for its smooth linear field. It imports no positivity or nonnormal matrix-stability conclusion.
The reversible-transfer example uses nonnegative off-diagonal entries, zero column sums, and source-column indexing exactly as defined by the finite column-generator supplier.

The counterexample substitutes ρ = 1 and h = 3/2 into the exact scalar interval 0 < hρ ≤ 2 and checks the zero eigenvalue separately. The supplier page reciprocally identifies positivity as a separate property.

This is a contextual page prerequisite: the sectional items do not import a Patankar theorem. Their selected forward-Euler procedure proves positivity through nonnegative event gains and hΛ_i ≤ 1, and proves augmented-mass conservation directly from event increments.
